commands.command: gh release list --limit 8 && for t in v0.16.0 v0.15.0 v0.14.0 v0.13.1 v0.13.0 v0.12.1; do gh release view "pantheon-base-$t" --json assets --jq '.assets | length'; done
commands.details: Establishes the break. v0.16.0, v0.15.0 and v0.14.0 each report 0 assets. v0.13.0 and v0.12.1 each report 4. The artifact channel broke at v0.14.0 and stayed broken for three consecutive releases, with no failing signal anywhere.

Recovers the intended artifact shape from the last release that worked: foundation-release-pantheon-base-v0.13.0.tgz (18229344 bytes), foundation-release-pantheon-base-v0.13.0.tgz.sha256 (111 bytes), repo.tar (30556160 bytes), repo.tar.sha256 (75 bytes). This four-asset set is what the new gate requires.

commands.command: cat pantheon-ops/foundation-release.lock.json (parsed: releaseVersion, sharedPaths) && ls pantheon-ops/.foundation/releases/
commands.details: Links the break to its consumer impact. The lock is pinned to pantheon-base-v0.13.0 and the materialized bundles stop at pantheon-base-v0.13.0. A lock cannot advance to a version that has no artifacts, so the missing assets are the direct cause of the ops baseline sitting three minor versions behind, not a coincidence.

Confirms the scripts exist and are unwired. package.json exposes release:foundation:bundle/cut/manifest/publish; the only workflow reference is ci.yml:186 running npm run test:foundation-release. No workflow ever runs publish, which is why releases after v0.13.0 were created by hand without assets.

Shows the documented contract disagreeing with the implemented gate. The header states the gate 'must pass before pantheon-base-vX.Y.Z is tagged and the release bundle is published', but no job in the file observes the published bundle.

Positive control, exit 0. '[ok] local bundle pantheon-base-v0.13.0: foundation-release-pantheon-base-v0.13.0.tgz, repo.tar' followed by '[ok] release pantheon-base-v0.13.0 carries all 4 required assets'. Also exercises the local bundle path: both archives' SHA-256 sidecars validate against the same validateReleaseAssetChecksum the publish path uses.

Negative control, exit 1. '[FAIL] release pantheon-base-v0.16.0 is missing assets: foundation-release-pantheon-base-v0.16.0.tgz, foundation-release-pantheon-base-v0.16.0.tgz.sha256, repo.tar, repo.tar.sha256'. This is the state that previously produced no signal at all.
Argument validation, exit 1 with 'release-version must match pantheon-base-vX.Y.Z' on stderr. Confirms the gate cannot be pointed at a bare semver and silently pass.

21/21 pass in 2.9s. Covers: the required asset set; a complete asset list accepted; each missing asset reported; an empty release reported as fully missing; a valid local bundle accepted; a tampered archive rejected on SHA-256 mismatch; a missing checksum sidecar rejected; an absent version directory reported as not present; local-only accepting a valid bundle without touching GitHub (asserted by a fetch spy that must not be called); local-only failing when no bundle was built; local-only plus skip-local rejected as contradictory; the complete-release pass path; the missing-asset fail path; release-not-found failing without waiting; the publish-in-flight retry succeeding on the second attempt with exactly one 5000ms sleep; unexpected errors rethrown rather than reported as a gate failure; malformed options rejected; --local-only and --dist parsed; the version-format rejection; and the missing --release-version rejection.
Confirms the npm script wiring, not just the direct node invocation. Exit 0 with the same two [ok] lines.

Result: PASS. The new script reuses validateReleaseAssetChecksum and isMissingGitHubReleaseError from publish-foundation-release.mjs instead of reimplementing checksum logic, so it adds no duplicated block above the 21-line detection floor. This was a design constraint: copying runCommand/parseRepoParts/resolveRepoFullName would have been a ~41-line contiguous duplicate.

commands.command: python -c "import yaml, re; ..." over .github/workflows/foundation-release-verify.yml and foundation-release-backfill.yml
commands.details: Both files parse as YAML. verify triggers on ['release','workflow_dispatch'] with top-level permissions contents:read and two jobs (verify-assets, summary with needs and if:always()); backfill triggers on ['workflow_dispatch'] only with contents:write scoped to the job. Every uses: entry matches /[^@]+@[0-9a-f]{40}/, so both workflows are SHA-pinned like the rest of the repository.

Hosted SonarCloud failed the PR quality gate as ERROR (new_security_rating 5 against a threshold of 1) with 5 BLOCKER githubactions:S7630 findings, all in .github/workflows/foundation-release-backfill.yml at lines 94, 95, 96, 101 and 124. Every one was a workflow input interpolated straight into a run block: --release-version "${{ inputs.release_version }}", --release-line "${{ inputs.release_line }}", --base-commit "${{ inputs.base_commit }}" and two further release_version reads. The quotes do not help, because GitHub expands the expression before the shell parses the line, so a value containing a double quote or $( ) breaks out. .github/workflows is inside the Sonar scope (.sonarcloud.properties excludes only scripts/**, frontend/scripts/**, database/** and frontend/src/i18n/resources/**), and the repository's own Workflow Security job passed on the same revision, so SonarCloud was the only signal that caught this.

commands.command: python -c "..." re-validating both workflows for run-block injection after the fix
commands.details: Fixed by moving all inputs into a job-level env block (RELEASE_VERSION, RELEASE_LINE, BASE_COMMIT, DRY_RUN) and reading them as shell variables, which is the pattern the workflow's own Validate inputs step already used. The dynamic working-directory on the upload step was replaced with a dist= variable so no path is built from an expression either. Re-validation asserts that no run block in either workflow interpolates ${{ inputs.* }} or ${{ github.event.* }}, that both files still parse as YAML, and that every uses: remains SHA-pinned; a release_line format check was added at the same time. The remaining ${{ inputs.* }} occurrences sit in concurrency.group, job env, with.ref and if: conditions, none of which are shell contexts.

commands.command: git worktree add --detach /tmp/v016-wt 3fe572f3244070ab14e304bc075017f20e86e9cd && node scripts/foundation-release/build-release-manifest.mjs --release-version pantheon-base-v0.16.0 --release-line release/0.16 --base-commit 3fe572f3...
commands.details: Backfill feasibility, step 1. Checking out the v0.16.0 release commit and running that era's manifest builder produces releases/pantheon-base-v0.16.0/{manifest.json,verification-summary.json,release-notes.md,upgrade-notes.md,consumer-impact.md}. The manifest builder does not shell out, so it runs on this host.

commands.command: python -c "..." verifying every manifest sharedPath exists at commit 3fe572f3
commands.details: Backfill feasibility, step 2. The generated manifest declares 52 sharedPaths (backend 4, frontend 46, docs 2) and 0 are missing at that commit. Since copyEntry throws on a missing shared path, this is the precondition that would have failed the rebuild; it does not. Recorded as 'bundle build should succeed'.

The rebuild itself could NOT be executed on this host, and this is recorded rather than hidden. build-release-bundle.mjs calls runGit -> spawnSync('git', ['rev-parse', ...]), which fails here with 'git rev-parse 3fe572f3...^{commit} failed' because Node cannot spawn subprocesses in this environment. A direct probe confirms the scope: spawnSync returns status null with error.code EBUSY for git, for node and even for echo. The same limitation already fails 17 of the 40 pre-existing foundation-release tests on this machine, on files this change does not touch, so it is environmental rather than a regression. This is why the backfill is delivered as a CI workflow and was verified statically instead of executed.

Baseline for the environment claim: 23 pass / 17 fail locally, all 17 from spawn EBUSY, on build-release-bundle/build-release-manifest/publish tests that this change does not modify. Establishes that the local spawn failure predates this work and is not caused by it.

Reports 'structure check failed to enumerate files: spawnSync git EBUSY' - the same environmental limitation, on a file this change does not touch. Hosted CI on ubuntu-latest is the authoritative run for the spawn-dependent gates.

runtimeGap: Node cannot spawn subprocesses on this host: spawnSync returns status null with error.code EBUSY for git, node and echo alike. Any release script that shells out (build-release-bundle.mjs via git rev-parse / git archive, and the spawn-based existing tests) therefore cannot run here. The backfill was consequently delivered as a CI workflow and verified statically - the manifest builds, and all 52 sharedPaths exist at the release commit - rather than executed end to end. The new gate's own tests were deliberately written to avoid spawning so they do run here; the CLI wiring is covered through an exported runCheckCli rather than a spawned process. Hosted CI on ubuntu-latest remains the only environment where the two new workflows are actually exercised.
knownGaps: The bundle rebuild was not executed end to end on this host: Node cannot spawn git here, so git rev-parse and git archive both fail with EBUSY. Feasibility for v0.16.0 is established statically (manifest generated, 52/52 sharedPaths present at commit 3fe572f3) rather than by producing the archive.

Neither new workflow has been exercised by GitHub Actions yet. release: published only fires on the default branch, so the verify workflow cannot run before this change is merged, and the backfill workflow defaults to dry_run. Their first hosted runs are post-merge.

The new workflow is not a required check. Branch protection is a maintainer decision, so a release published without assets will go red but will not block on its own until the check is added to the required set.

Repairing v0.14.0, v0.15.0 and v0.16.0 is not part of this change. The backfill workflow enables it, but uploading to already-published releases is a deliberate operation that should be dispatched and reviewed separately.

The gate asserts the presence and checksum of the four assets. It does not verify that the bundle's contents match the release manifest's sharedPaths, which build-release-bundle.mjs already validates at build time.
Local execution of the spawn-dependent repository gates (check:structure, the 17 spawn-based release tests) is impossible on this host, so those remain CI-only signals for this change.

The 5 BLOCKER githubactions:S7630 findings were surfaced by hosted SonarCloud only after the PR was opened; no local gate caught them. The repository's Workflow Security job passed on the same revision, actionlint could not be installed on this host, and scripts/** is excluded from Sonar analysis so the new script was never scanned. The workflow was corrected and re-validated locally, but that re-validation is a Python assertion over the YAML rather than the Sonar rule engine, so the authoritative confirmation is the SonarCloud re-run against the pushed fix.
